questions.IDENTITY_EQUALITY: For the two mark assertions, determine whether their subjects identify the same immutable referent and whether their asserted values are equal. Report both Boolean fields independently; equality of values does not establish identity, and unequal values do not disprove identity.
questions.CURRENTNESS: Does the first listed trial observation belong to the explicitly deployed build? Answer CURRENT or NOT_CURRENT. Determine temporal applicability only.
questions.KNOWN_VS_UNKNOWN: Is the first listed trial input value uniquely determined by its reported_input and admissible_inputs? Answer KNOWN if exactly one input remains, otherwise UNKNOWN. An uncaptured singleton domain determines the value. Do not infer an input by assuming observed outputs obey requirements.
questions.CONTRADICTION: Can the two equal-standing mark assertions both hold for their specified immutable subjects? Answer CONSISTENT or CONTRADICTORY. Distinct builds, stations or cycles denote distinct subjects; duplicate agreeing assertions can coexist.
questions.ALTERNATIVE_COMPLETION_EXISTENCE: For the first listed trial, does any completion different from reference_input remain compatible with reported_input and admissible_inputs? Answer ALTERNATIVE_EXISTS or NO_ALTERNATIVE. This is an existence question, independent of whether required outputs agree. Do not infer input from output.
questions.OBSERVATION_REQUIREMENT_COMPARISON: For the first listed trial at its reference_input completion, is observed_result exactly equal to the supplied required_results value? Answer MATCH or MISMATCH. Use the supplied value; perform no additional operational computation.
questions.EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY: Using only the deployment and trial facts, is the truth value of "the deployed trial observation differs from the required output for its actual input" uniquely determined? Answer DETERMINATE if all remaining admissible inputs give the same truth value, otherwise UNDERDETERMINED. The separate mark assertions do not constrain trial inputs. Do not infer inputs by presuming observed outputs obey requirements.

pairs.semantic_delta: Change only the second assertion cycle to the next event; agreeing values remain equal.
